title: Anthropic's Claude Code had a workspace trust bypass (CVE-2026-33068). Not a prompt injection or AI attack. A configurat

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: This was a configuration flaw, not a prompt injection. The model didn't misinterpret input—it was a misconfigured trust boundary. (3 sec)

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: It was a loading order bug in the workspace config. The AI didn’t attack—it was a flaw in how Claude Code loaded external modules. Fixed in 2.1.53. (5 sec)

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: The vulnerability stemmed from workspace trust settings, not the model’s understanding. Prompt injection requires manipulation of the model’s input, which didn’t happen. (5 sec)

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: This is a safety win for AI, not a failure. The attack vector was a config error—proving that even the best systems need rigorous loading order validation. (5 sec)

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: A config bug, not an AI attack. A clear win for secure software design. (4 sec)

caption_text: Not a prompt injection vs AI attack. A configuration loading order bug. Fixed in 2.1.53.     An interesting data point in the AI safety discussion
